entries.description: The protected-change workflow triggers on pull_request_target, checks out a ref that is not the pull request head, does not npm install or run a script from the fetched ref, and its permissions are contents read, pull-requests read, and issues read, with issues write only on the label job.
A pull request head that rewrites protected-change.mjs to exit 0 and adds DROP TABLE still fails when the sensor entry point runs from the base checkout.
A pull request head that removes DROP\s+TABLE from harness.yaml and adds a DROP TABLE line still fails because the decision reads the base harness.yaml.
ci.yml does not run protected-change, and --status lists it as running from the base-branch workflow.
A mocked rules API with no rules on the default branch reports every expected rule missing. warn exits 0 and prints each one. block exits 1.
A pull request rule with dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push false makes the sensor name that parameter.
Output always contains the line that the bypass list is not visible to this token, and never calls the bypass list safe.
A rule type the sensor cannot map is reported as unknown and is never a pass.
A missing token or a GitHub API error exits 2.
With GH_TOKEN set, session start names GH_TOKEN in the session output and in report.json under credentials, and never prints the value.
With a fake gh on PATH that reports a logged-in account, the session start warning names the gh login.
With none of the credential markers and no .env, session start prints no known credentials visible and names what it cannot see.
The credentials warning does not change the exit code of session start.
doc-drift fails when a setting name in docs/platform-gates.md or docs/agent-identity.md has no cited doc URL on the same line.
No file in the repo contains the old turn-mode claim about an agent commit, or the old course-map claim about an integrity check.
The failure-modes table has a Prevents or warns column, every row is filled, and hook or pattern rows say warns.
doc-drift stays green, and the README says the review panel and any hosted AI reviewer are advisory and that their approval never counts.
The protected-change workflow has no pull_request or pull_request_review trigger.
DROP TABLE outside every protected path fails until a code owner label is added after the latest push. A pull request that only touches a protected path reports that the ruleset decides and exits 0.
